doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Grimes's parents and the piano at home
summary: Grimes knows little about his parents' music beyond the piano in the house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me ask you about growing up in Philadelphia. Henry, I think I heard that your parents were musicians.

Yes, as much as I know about it is mainly hearsay. Because I came to hear music in the house it was when I realized that we had a piano, so I used to play it, and nobody else. My brother maybe, but I don’t think he did too much though, but I did a little bit, and I never found out of they were really musicians or not.
You don’t know why they sort of got out of the business.
No I don’t. But I mean it seemed like a very — in fact they must have known some professional bearing years before.
You know what became popular, I mean not popular but given over to musical, professional life.
